units.title: Unit 1: Classical Greece & Rome to Medieval Europe

lessons.title: Part 1: Classical Greece & Rome — Democracy, Republic & Law
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Classical Greece and the Roman Republic
lessons.reading: Mountainous geography divided Greece into independent city-states. Athens pioneered direct democracy, where citizens voted directly on laws. Rome created a republic with elected representatives, written laws (the Twelve Tables), and engineering marvels like stone arches and aqueducts.

principles.title: Classical Greece & Rome: Democracy, Republic, Law & Engineering
principles.summary: Greek democracy and Roman republican law and engineering shaped modern civilization.

bank.prompt: What form of government did ancient Athens develop?
bank.explanation: Direct democracy is a system where citizens vote directly on laws and public decisions.

bank.prompt: How did the Roman Republic govern its citizens?
choices: One pharaoh ruled as a god
bank.explanation: A republic is a government in which citizens elect representatives to make laws for them.

bank.prompt: What were the Twelve Tables in ancient Rome?
bank.explanation: The Twelve Tables were Rome’s first published laws, establishing that law applies to all citizens.

bank.prompt: What did Roman aqueducts transport into cities?
bank.explanation: Aqueducts were bridge-like stone channels engineered by Romans to carry fresh water to cities.

bank.prompt: Why did mountains and islands matter in ancient Greece?
choices: They separated Greece into independent city-states
They created one giant flat desert
bank.answer: They separated Greece into independent city-states
bank.explanation: A polis (city-state) was an independent Greek city and its surrounding land, separated by mountains.

bank.prompt: Which architectural feature allowed Romans to build strong bridges and domes?
bank.explanation: Roman engineers used arches and concrete to support heavy weight across wide spaces.

bank.prompt: How did Alexander the Great spread Hellenistic culture?
choices: Blending Greek ideas with Persian and Egyptian cultures
Closing all libraries and trade routes
bank.answer: Blending Greek ideas with Persian and Egyptian cultures
bank.explanation: Hellenistic culture blended Greek art, science, and philosophy with cultures across Southwest Asia and Egypt.

bank.prompt: Which Greek thinkers used logic and reason to study the world?
bank.explanation: Philosophy is the search for wisdom using logic, observation, and questioning.

lessons.title: Part 2: Medieval Europe — Feudalism, Manors & the Magna Carta
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Feudalism, Serfdom & the Magna Carta
lessons.reading: After Rome fell, European nobles used feudalism—exchanging land (fiefs) for military service from knights—while peasant serfs farmed self-sufficient manors. Later, the Crusades expanded trade, the Black Death created labor shortages, and England’s Magna Carta (1215) limited royal power under the law.

principles.title: Medieval Europe: Feudalism, Manorialism & the Magna Carta
principles.summary: Feudalism exchanged land for loyalty, while the Magna Carta limited royal power.

bank.prompt: What was feudalism in medieval Europe?
choices: Exchanging land for military service and loyalty
Voting for a president every four years
Paying taxes only in paper money
bank.answer: Exchanging land for military service and loyalty
bank.explanation: Feudalism was a medieval system where nobles gave land (fiefs) to vassals in exchange for loyalty.

bank.prompt: What was the role of serfs on a medieval manor?
choices: Farmed the lord’s land in exchange for protection
bank.answer: Farmed the lord’s land in exchange for protection
bank.explanation: Manorialism was the economic system where peasant serfs farmed a lord’s estate for shelter and safety.

bank.prompt: Why was the Magna Carta of 1215 important?
choices: It limited the power of the English king
It ended all farming in Europe
bank.answer: It limited the power of the English king
bank.explanation: The Magna Carta established that even the monarch must obey the law and respect basic rights.

bank.prompt: Who were knights in the feudal system?
choices: Mounted warriors who pledged to defend a lord
bank.answer: Mounted warriors who pledged to defend a lord
bank.explanation: Knights were armored warriors who received land from lords in return for military service.

bank.prompt: How did the Black Death affect medieval Europe?
choices: Caused labor shortages that weakened feudalism
Doubled the population of every city
bank.answer: Caused labor shortages that weakened feudalism
bank.explanation: The bubonic plague killed millions, allowing surviving workers to demand wages and weaken feudal ties.

bank.prompt: What economic effect did the Crusades have on Europe?
choices: Increased trade between Europe and Southwest Asia
Ended the use of gold coins
bank.answer: Increased trade between Europe and Southwest Asia
bank.explanation: The Crusades brought Europeans into contact with Asian silks, spices, and scientific knowledge.

bank.prompt: What was a fief in medieval society?
choices: A grant of land given to a vassal
A stone tower inside a castle
A tax paid to a guild
bank.answer: A grant of land given to a vassal
bank.explanation: A fief was an estate of land granted by a lord to a vassal in return for sworn loyalty.

bank.prompt: How did monasteries preserve learning during the Middle Ages?
choices: Monks copied and saved ancient manuscripts
bank.answer: Monks copied and saved ancient manuscripts
bank.explanation: Medieval monasteries served as centers of literacy where monks hand-copied classical and religious texts.

units.title: Unit 2: Renaissance, Reformation & Global Trade Empires

lessons.title: Part 1: The Renaissance, Gutenberg Press & the Reformation
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: The Italian Renaissance & Protestant Reformation
lessons.reading: Wealthy Italian trading cities sparked the Renaissance, a rebirth of classical art, science, and humanism. Johannes Gutenberg’s movable-type printing press made books affordable and helped spread Martin Luther’s Reformation ideas across Europe.

principles.title: The Renaissance, Gutenberg Press & the Reformation
principles.summary: The Renaissance revived classical learning while the printing press spread Reformation ideas.

bank.prompt: What does the word "Renaissance" mean?
bank.explanation: The Renaissance was a cultural rebirth in Europe that revived Greek and Roman art and inquiry.

bank.prompt: Why did the Renaissance begin in Italian city-states like Florence?
choices: Wealthy trade merchants funded artists and scholars
Italy had no access to sea trade
Feudal serfs owned all Italian banks
bank.answer: Wealthy trade merchants funded artists and scholars
bank.explanation: Patrons were wealthy merchant families who sponsored painters, sculptors, and humanist thinkers.

bank.prompt: What did Renaissance humanism emphasize?
choices: Human potential, reason, and classical education
bank.answer: Human potential, reason, and classical education
bank.explanation: Humanism focused on the value of human achievement, literature, history, and observation.

bank.prompt: How did Johannes Gutenberg’s printing press change Europe?
choices: Made books cheaper and spread literacy rapidly
Made books ten times more expensive
Forced people to write on clay
bank.answer: Made books cheaper and spread literacy rapidly
bank.explanation: Movable-type printing allowed books to be produced quickly, spreading new religious and scientific ideas.

bank.prompt: Who started the Protestant Reformation in 1517 with his Ninety-Five Theses?
bank.explanation: The Reformation was a religious movement started by Martin Luther to reform church practices.

bank.prompt: What church practice did Martin Luther strongly criticize?
bank.explanation: Luther argued that salvation could not be bought with money through certificates called indulgences.

bank.prompt: Who painted the Mona Lisa and filled notebooks with inventions?
bank.explanation: Leonardo da Vinci was a "Renaissance man" skilled in painting, anatomy, and engineering.

bank.prompt: How did translating the Bible into everyday languages affect people?
choices: Ordinary citizens could read scripture themselves
Only kings were allowed to read
Latin became the only spoken tongue
bank.answer: Ordinary citizens could read scripture themselves
bank.explanation: Vernacular translations let everyday people read books in their own native language.

lessons.title: Part 2: West African Empires, Islamic Golden Age & Global Exchange
lessons.videoTitle: Khan Academy: Mali Empire, Silk Road & Columbian Exchange
lessons.reading: In West Africa, the empires of Ghana and Mali (led by Mansa Musa) flourished on the gold-salt trade and turned Timbuktu into a center of learning. Scholars of the Islamic Golden Age advanced algebra and medicine, Silk Road caravans linked Eurasia, and the Columbian Exchange connected the Americas and Afro-Eurasia.

principles.title: West African Empires, Islamic Golden Age & Global Exchange
principles.summary: Trans-Saharan gold-salt trade, Silk Road networks, and the Columbian Exchange reshaped the world.

bank.prompt: Which two goods drove trade in West Africa’s Ghana and Mali empires?
bank.explanation: West African empires grew wealthy by taxing the trans-Saharan trade of gold and desert salt.

bank.prompt: Which Mali ruler made a famous pilgrimage and supported Timbuktu schools?
bank.explanation: Mansa Musa ruled Mali and turned Timbuktu into a major center of Islamic learning and trade.

bank.prompt: What were scholars in the Islamic Golden Age known for advancing?
bank.explanation: During the Islamic Golden Age, scholars in cities like Baghdad advanced math, medicine, and optics.

bank.prompt: What was the Silk Road?
choices: Trade routes linking China to the Mediterranean
bank.answer: Trade routes linking China to the Mediterranean
bank.explanation: The Silk Road was a network of overland trade routes carrying goods and ideas across Eurasia.

bank.prompt: What was the Columbian Exchange?
choices: Transfer of plants, animals, and diseases across the Atlantic
A treaty between Athens and Sparta
A gold coin used in Mali
bank.answer: Transfer of plants, animals, and diseases across the Atlantic
bank.explanation: The Columbian Exchange moved crops, livestock, people, and diseases between the Americas and Afro-Eurasia.

bank.prompt: Which crops traveled from the Americas to Europe in the Columbian Exchange?
bank.explanation: American crops like potatoes and maize (corn) boosted food supplies and populations in Europe.

bank.prompt: How did Old World diseases affect Indigenous peoples in the Americas?
bank.explanation: Indigenous populations lacked immunity to smallpox and measles, leading to catastrophic losses.

bank.prompt: Which animal brought from Europe transformed life on the Great Plains?
bank.explanation: Europeans reintroduced horses to the Americas, changing travel and hunting for Indigenous nations.

bank.prompt: Who started the Protestant Reformation in 1517 with his Ninety-Five Theses?
bank.explanation: The Reformation was a religious movement started by Martin Luther to reform church practices.

bank.prompt: What church practice did Martin Luther strongly criticize?
bank.explanation: Luther argued that salvation could not be bought with money through certificates called indulgences.

bank.prompt: Who painted the Mona Lisa and filled notebooks with inventions?
bank.explanation: Leonardo da Vinci was a "Renaissance man" skilled in painting, anatomy, and engineering.

bank.prompt: How did translating the Bible into everyday languages affect people?
choices: Ordinary citizens could read scripture themselves
Only kings were allowed to read
Latin became the only spoken tongue
bank.answer: Ordinary citizens could read scripture themselves
bank.explanation: Vernacular translations let everyday people read books in their own native language.

principles.title: West African Empires, Islamic Golden Age & Global Exchange
principles.summary: Trans-Saharan gold-salt trade, Silk Road networks, and the Columbian Exchange reshaped the world.

bank.prompt: Which two goods drove trade in West Africa’s Ghana and Mali empires?
bank.explanation: West African empires grew wealthy by taxing the trans-Saharan trade of gold and desert salt.

bank.prompt: Which Mali ruler made a famous pilgrimage and supported Timbuktu schools?
bank.explanation: Mansa Musa ruled Mali and turned Timbuktu into a major center of Islamic learning and trade.

bank.prompt: What were scholars in the Islamic Golden Age known for advancing?
bank.explanation: During the Islamic Golden Age, scholars in cities like Baghdad advanced math, medicine, and optics.

bank.prompt: What was the Silk Road?
choices: Trade routes linking China to the Mediterranean
bank.answer: Trade routes linking China to the Mediterranean
bank.explanation: The Silk Road was a network of overland trade routes carrying goods and ideas across Eurasia.

bank.prompt: What was the Columbian Exchange?
choices: Transfer of plants, animals, and diseases across the Atlantic
A treaty between Athens and Sparta
A gold coin used in Mali
bank.answer: Transfer of plants, animals, and diseases across the Atlantic
bank.explanation: The Columbian Exchange moved crops, livestock, people, and diseases between the Americas and Afro-Eurasia.

bank.prompt: Which crops traveled from the Americas to Europe in the Columbian Exchange?
bank.explanation: American crops like potatoes and maize (corn) boosted food supplies and populations in Europe.

bank.prompt: How did Old World diseases affect Indigenous peoples in the Americas?
bank.explanation: Indigenous populations lacked immunity to smallpox and measles, leading to catastrophic losses.

bank.prompt: Which animal brought from Europe transformed life on the Great Plains?
bank.explanation: Europeans reintroduced horses to the Americas, changing travel and hunting for Indigenous nations.
